lens: Security — attack surface, OWASP class, DoS, secrets, audit chain, supply chain
answer: PR #12 is a path-only hygiene rename plus a .gitignore + git-rm --cached for a session-scoped audit log; it does not change admission policy semantics, does not introduce new attack surface, and does not touch tenant data or live secrets. The kyverno ClusterPolicy (cosign keyless + Rekor) and the Argo Application (prune/selfHeal, repoURL pinned to the canonical fork, path: infra/kyverno/oya-vcs-admission) are byte-for-byte preserved except for the rewritten path, and the kernel's validate_argo_application invariants were updated in lockstep to assert the new path. The only material security observations are (a) the untracked .audit/agent-read.jsonl still exists in git history across 8 commits (the rm --cached does not scrub it — but the captured content is only file-path arguments to git log/read, no token/credential material), and (b) the rewritten Argo Application omits an explicit metadata.namespace.app.kubernetes.io/managed-by pinning and the Application name retains the `-preview` suffix in a path now branded as the canonical admission root, which are low-severity ergonomics rather than vulnerabilities.
key_claims: ARGO_MANIFEST in tools/oya-foundry-vcs-provider-execution-gate-app/src/main.rs and the three expected_scalar_fields in the kernel both correctly point to 'infra/kyverno/oya-vcs-admission(/application.json)'; manifest + validator are consistent.
Self-referential spec.source.path inside application.json was rewritten to 'infra/kyverno/oya-vcs-admission'; Argo will resolve the new repo path correctly, no GitOps drift.

evidence/multispectrum/oya-vcs-provider-execution-proof-1778845600.json, evidence/gitops-vcs/oya-vcs-admission-cutover-2026-05-15.json (2 hits), and evidence/gitops-vcs/provider-execution-proof-2026-05-15.json (1 hit) all point to the new infra/kyverno/ location at merge commit 70b83631; no stale deploy/gitops/ references survive in tracked files; deploy/ tree is fully removed from the tree at merge.

git rm --cached .audit/agent-read.jsonl removes it from the working tree only; the blob remains reachable from 8 prior commits including merges. Content scan (bearer/authorization/aws_/ghp_/ghs_/sk_live/cookies/private-key markers) returns zero hits — the file is structured EVT-AGENT-READ-* records whose payloads are file-path argv arrays, not secret values. References to 'crates/oya-secrets-*' inside the log are source-tree paths, not secret material.

Kyverno ClusterPolicy require-signed-oyatie-images was not touched by this PR — it still enforces cosign keyless verification against token.actions.githubusercontent.com with Rekor transparency at rekor.sigstore.dev for ghcr.io/oyatie/* image references; supply-chain posture is unchanged.
ADR-0117 is Accepted and accurately documents the move + the CI-driven decision to keep .config/nextest.toml tracked.
.gitignore now contains '.audit/'; future agent-read logs will not be re-committed, closing the recurrence vector.
uncertainty_areas: Whether the Argo Application's metadata.name='oya-vcs-admission-preview' is intentional (preview channel) or stale labelling now that the manifest lives under the canonical infra/kyverno/ root — out of this PR's stated scope.

Whether any external/non-tracked GitOps tooling (e.g., an Argo ApplicationSet, Flux Kustomization, or out-of-repo automation) still resolves to deploy/gitops/oya-vcs-admission; only in-repo references were verified.

Whether the previously committed .audit/agent-read.jsonl blob should be BFG/filter-repo scrubbed from history — content review shows no secret material, so the cost/risk of a force-rewrite likely outweighs the benefit, but this is a policy judgment call.
anti_patterns_detected: git rm --cached without an explicit decision recorded on whether to scrub history — acceptable here because the content is non-sensitive, but the ADR should state this explicitly so future agents do not assume history-rewrite occurred.

findings.summary: .audit/agent-read.jsonl remains in git history (8 prior commits) after rm --cached; ADR-0117 does not explicitly assert non-sensitivity of the historical blob.
findings.recommended_action: Append a one-line note to ADR-0117 stating 'historical blob scanned; contains only EVT-AGENT-READ-* file-path argv records, no secrets; history-rewrite intentionally not performed' so future auditors do not re-open the question.

findings.summary: Argo Application metadata.namespace is pinned to 'argocd' and spec.destination.namespace to 'oyatie-system', but metadata.name still carries the '-preview' suffix while the path is now branded as the canonical admission root.
findings.recommended_action: Out-of-scope for this PR. Track in a follow-up to either rename to 'oya-vcs-admission' (production) or document the preview-channel intent in ADR-0117 / a successor ADR.

findings.summary: Kyverno ClusterPolicy is cluster-scoped (no namespace pinning), which is correct for ClusterPolicy kind; no action needed.
findings.recommended_action: No action — flagged only to confirm the security reviewer evaluated namespace pinning per the prompt.
